Welcome to Summerfields Primary School
Welcome to our school website; I hope it will give you an insight into the many opportunities that we offer our children whilst also providing lots of helpful information about the school. Summerfields is a relatively small school tucked away in Newport; whilst being just a short walk from the town. The children benefit from fantastic grounds and lots of space!
Everyone here works as part of the Summerfields team and we are extremely proud of the friendly and welcoming feel of the school. We are also proud of the positive and active role the children have in school life and of the partnerships we enjoy with our parent community. We aspire to always "Be the best we can be".
As well as supporting our children to achieve their best academically, at Summerfields Primary School we aim to foster a spirit of belonging and caring for others. We believe it is equally important to help children to flourish as confident and happy young people, ready for life beyond the school gates.
If you would like to see Summerfields Primary in action or have any other questions, please do not hesitate to contact us; it is always a pleasure to welcome parents and visitors to our school.
Mrs Melanie Gartell, Headteacher
Our values, beliefs and visions
Our Values help us to achieve our motto
"be the best we can be"
At Summerfields Primary School children come first and every child matters. We are inclusive and recognise that everyone has the right be heard and to be taught in a safe environment. Children and adults should never give up, team work enables us to overcome challenges so that we can all be the best we can be. There are three core values at Summerfields that are easy as ABC for the children to remember.
Our Vision, or why do we exist?
To provide an inclusive, nurturing school where children achieve well, enjoy their learning and acquire skills they need to succeed in a changing world.

Curriculum
Curriculum Approach
At Summerfields Primary each learning experience is focused around just one area of the curriculum. This allows children time to explore and develop key knowledge and skills in these areas. It also gives the opportunity to focus on what being a historian is like, what does it mean to be a geographer, what do designers do etc.
Reading and writing underpin the learning experiences and are used as tools to communicate the key concepts to a wider audience.
There are a range of ways used to begin a new subject. This allows the teacher to review previous learning and provide the opportunity to ensure that the steps of learning are personalised and take into account the starting points of the children to achieve the highest possible quality outcomes.
Children receive feedback during their learning which enables them to know their next step of learning - for example, what is the single thing that will make the biggest difference to them progressing as a writer. At other key moments during the learning experience, staff use their professional judgement to give meaningful feedback about a child’s next steps in learning - this may be given in a variety of ways: small group, verbal, 1:1 conferencing or written.
We recognise that successful learners are determined, courageous, positive and reflective. They also take pride in their achievements. The nurture and development of these behaviours underpins our core values - achieve, belong and care, which are also at the forefront of curriculum planning as well as everyday life in school.

Our curriculum mapping tool holds our school vision at its core.
It is bespoke to meet the needs of Summerfields Primary School and will be continually reviewed and refined. It is both brave and ambitious. It includes the National Curriculum and aims to secure a robust approach to the development of knowledge and skills in all areas of the curriculum.

Curriculum
At Summerfields Primary School, all children have access to a wide curriculum which includes English, Maths, Science, Computing, Geography, History, Music, Art, Technology, PSHE and PE. We follow a locally agreed syllabus for RE. Most emphasis is placed on English, Maths, Science and Computing.

EYFS Curriculum Overview
Year 1
Pedagogy for continuous provision in Year 1 at Summerfields:
At Summerfields Primary School, we have found a way to ensure that every one of the 30 children in Year 1 has access to an education that is uniquely suited to them as individual learners, where they are also becoming co-operative and responsible members of the school society. They are equipped with the literacy and maths skills that they need in order to "play" and learn about things that interest them. Through this they will thrive – they have remained enthusiastic, independent, happy and unique individuals. Children aged five or six want to learn. Moreover, they want to be active, autonomous and unique learners – exploring, discovering, creating and taking risks. In other words they want to play. They each have different life histories, leading to unique personalities, interests, needs and skills. But they all want to play in order to satisfy their desire to learn.
Whole class teaching will be appropriate at times, for example teacher input for maths and phonics. Children’s work will be recorded in a variety of ways but always appropriate for the child’s level of development and in line with National Curriculum expectations. As the year progresses there will be greater emphasis on adult led activities which will prepare the children for their transition into Year 2.
